en: A state from which the power has been taken to defend itself against foreign states, which has no power inwardly either to administer the highest justice or to preserve its rights over the whole against the individuals who seize those rights for themselves, must necessarily in war be exposed [to] all plunderings and devastations, bear the chief costs of it, which friend and foe has, lose provinces to foreign powers; it must leave justice to politics and to fate, and, with state power annihilated over the individual members and supremacy over the vassals lost, enclose within itself nothing but sovereign states, of which, according to the bare law of power and prudence, the stronger expand and the weaker are swallowed up; such a state must fall into the condition before the peace of the land, only that this condition looks more peaceful through the altered character of men and instruments of violence.
zh: 一个被夺去了抵御外邦之力的国家，一个对内既没有力量主持最高司法、也没有力量保住自己对整体的权利不被那些把这些权利据为己有的个人侵夺的国家，在战争中就必然要遭受一切劫掠和破坏，承担战争的主要费用——这费用敌我双方都有——，把一些省份丢给外邦势力；它必然要把正义交给政治和命运去处置，并且在国家权力对各个成员已经毁灭、对封臣的宗主权已经丧失的情况下，自身之内除了些主权国家之外再也包不住别的东西，而这些主权国家按照赤裸裸的权力和精明的法则，强大的就扩张，弱小的就被吞掉；这样一个国家必然陷进国内和平之前的那种状态，只不过由于人的性格和暴力工具的改变，这种状态看上去要和平一些。

en: A. Germany's fate with respect to foreign powers
zh: A. 德意志面对外邦势力的命运

en: The lands that the German Empire has lost in the course of several centuries make up a long, sad list; and the teachers of state law still plume themselves greatly on the great claims that Germany has, and set them forth with just the same consoling emotion with which an impoverished nobleman preserves the paintings of his ancestors, the last remnant of his vanished greatness; both are equally little disturbed in their consolation.

The claims of the scholars of state law have never yet awakened anxiety in any minister, and after the paintings of the noble ancestors neither are the creditors eager, nor does the owner himself come into temptation to sell them, because the price would stand far too far below the value; and those claims as well as these pictures moulder quietly away together.
Sometimes the owners give themselves the pleasure of dusting them off and procuring for themselves an innocent delight in contemplating them.
zh: 德意志帝国在几百年间陆续失去的那些地方，组成了一份长长的、令人悲伤的清单；而国家法教师们至今还大为得意于德意志所拥有的那些巨大要求，并且带着一种令人慰藉的感动把它们一一列举出来，那感动就像一个破了产的贵族保存他祖先的画像、保存他那已经消逝的伟大的最后一点遗存时所怀的一样；两者在各自的慰藉中受到的打扰同样地少。
国家法学者的那些要求还从来没有让哪一个大臣感到过不安，而对于那些贵族祖先的画像，债主们并不垂涎，所有者自己也起不了把它们卖掉的念头，因为价钱会比价值低得太多；那些要求和这些画像就这样一起安安静静地发霉。
有时候，所有者们会给自己找点乐趣，把它们掸去灰尘，在端详它们当中给自己弄到一种无害的愉悦。

en: If there should still be talk among the teachers of state law of claims of the German Empire to Hungary, Poland, Prussia, Naples, etc., then not a word is to be lost about their political unimportance.

But also with regard to the former state-connection of these lands it is to be remarked that they were not in connection with the German state, but with the Roman emperor, in his former capacity as head of Christendom, lord of the world, etc., and that this connection does not concern the German state; that the Roman emperor and king in Germany, as it is still separated in the title, was in essence separated; and the German Empire had neither the interest and the will nor the power to maintain what could be counted as belonging to the dominion of the Roman emperor, and such an unnatural union of lands; yet it could not and would not preserve as integrating parts of itself those states that stood in an actual state-connection with it.
zh: 如果国家法教师那里还在谈论德意志帝国对匈牙利、波兰、普鲁士、那不勒斯等等的要求，那么关于这些要求在政治上的无足轻重，就一个字也不必多说了。

但即使就这些地方过去的国家联系而言，也要指出：它们并不是和德意志国家相联系，而是和罗马皇帝相联系，是和他从前作为基督教界之首、世界之主等等的身份相联系，所以这种联系与德意志国家毫不相干；罗马皇帝和在日耳曼的国王，正如在头衔里至今仍然是分开的那样，在本质上本来就是分开的；而德意志帝国既没有兴趣、没有意愿，也没有力量去维持那些可以算作罗马皇帝统治之下的东西、维持这样一种不自然的诸地方联合，然而对于那些与它处在真正的国家联系中的国家，它却既不能、也不愿把它们当作自己的整合部分保留下来。

en: The Lombard kingdom stood in a closer relation to Germany, and traces of it have been preserved down to the most recent times, but these traces are still weaker [than the relations] in which the German estates stand with the Empire, and can therefore not come into consideration with regard to the state.
zh: 伦巴德王国与德意志的关系更为紧密，直到最近的时代还保存着它的一些痕迹，但这些痕迹比德意志各等级与帝国所处的关系还要微弱，因此就国家而言不能列入考虑。

en: As for the lands essentially belonging to the German Empire and possessing full imperial estatehood, almost every war of the Empire has ended for it with the loss of such estates; this loss comprehends two kinds within itself; namely, apart from the subjugation of German lands under foreign supremacy and their complete tearing loose from all rights and duties toward the Empire, apart from this loss of Germany it must be regarded as a loss for the state that so many lands indeed remained in all their previous legal relation to emperor and Empire, but received princes who are at the same time monarchs of independent realms.

It is this circumstance that is seemingly no loss, that seemingly left everything as of old, [but] has undermined the coherence of the state in its foundation pillars, because these lands have thereby become independent of the executive power of the German state, of the state power.
zh: 至于那些本质上属于德意志帝国、拥有完整的帝国等级身份的地方，帝国几乎每一场战争都以它失去这样的等级而告终；这种失去本身包含两类情形；也就是说，除了德意志的地方屈服于外邦的宗主权之下、彻底脱离对帝国的一切权利和义务之外，除了德意志的这一损失之外，还必须看作国家之损失的是：有那么多地方虽然在其以往对皇帝和帝国的一切法权关系上都保持原样，却得到了同时是独立王国君主的诸侯。
正是这一情形，表面上并不是什么损失，表面上让一切都照旧，却挖空了国家联结的根基，因为这些地方由此就摆脱了德意志国家的执行权力、摆脱了国家权力而独立了。

en: Without going back to older times, we will give an overview of how, from the Peace of Westphalia onward, the powerlessness of Germany, its fate in relation to foreign powers and the extent of its territory have expressed themselves; of what Germany's loss through the peace has been; for the damage through the war itself is too immeasurable for any statement.181)
zh: 不追溯更早的时代，我们想概述一下：从《威斯特伐利亚和约》起，德意志的无力、它在与外邦势力的关系中的命运以及它疆域的范围是怎样表现出来的；德意志通过和约所受的损失是什么；因为战争本身造成的损害，对任何陈述来说都太不可估量了。181)

en: d. political principle, in order to let the great ones feel their dependence
zh: d. 政治原则，为了让大人物们感觉到自己的依赖性

en: II.
If then also a definitive judgment has been issued, execution is lacking; from this side the anarchy is visible, no state power.
zh: II.
即使随后作出了确定的判决，也缺少执行；从这一方面看，无政府状态是显而易见的，根本没有国家权力。

en: III.

The sovereign rights of the princes indeed do not extend to war and peace — in more recent times also, according to practice — but to alliances with foreign powers; thereby the rights of the estates [become] objects of politics, in any case and by right.

Precisely this tendency to independence makes all improvement impossible; a well-grounded pretext — bad justice, in order to withdraw from it; that tendency cannot remove the pretext; the Visitation under Joseph II.
The estates, attacked, attacked the emperor and Mainz, both therefore let it go on; both [were] disgusted, because their indeterminate rights could lose through being determined.

To the imperial estates a better justice would be terrible, [it] destroys their politics, the sending of envoys to foreign powers, acquisition through political negotiations, both stand in complete contradiction; what is a matter of right cannot be a matter of power, of influence, etc.
The estates indeed do not have the right of war with one another, but mediately through alliances; the city of Münster was thus brought under the bishopric.
zh: III.
诸侯的主权权利虽然并不扩展到战争与和平——在较近的时代，按实际做法也是这样——，而是扩展到与外部势力结盟；由此各等级的权利就成了政治的对象，无论按事情本身还是按法权都是如此。
正是这种走向独立的趋向使一切改善都不可能；有根据的借口——糟糕的司法，好借它来摆脱这种趋向；那种趋向并不能取消这个借口；约瑟夫二世治下的巡视。
各等级受到攻击，就去攻击皇帝和美因茨，双方于是都听任事情发展；双方都感到厌恶，因为他们那些不确定的权利可能由于被确定下来而受损。
对帝国各等级来说，一种更好的司法是可怕的，它会毁掉他们的政治、派使节去外部势力那里、通过政治谈判来获取，而这两者处在完全的矛盾之中；属于权利的事情，不可能是权力、影响等等的事情。
各等级之间虽然没有战争的权利，却通过结盟而间接地有了这种权利；明斯特城就是这样被弄到主教区之下的。

en: IV.

A very important circumstance, however, is the difference that takes place between state power and object of right; an object of right is a private property; state power cannot be private property; it flows from the state; there is no right to it except that of the state; its extent, the possession of it, depends on the state, valid only in relation to it; no object of judicial treatment.
Acquisition of private property is a matter of chance, of arbitrariness.

State power must stand in the closest connection with the whole; the state is the highest lord — even if only in one respect — of the defence of the laws, and against the outside, however — so at least herein, all right proceeds from it, it has to decide, not chance, not documents, and other titles of right.
zh: IV.
但一个很重要的情况是，国家权力和法权对象之间存在的区别；法权对象是一种私有财产；国家权力不能是私有财产；它从国家流出；除国家之外，谁也没有对它的权利；它的范围、对它的占有都取决于国家，只在与国家相关时才有效；它不是司法处理的对象。
私有财产的获得是偶然、是任意的事情。
国家权力必须与整体处在最紧密的联系之中；国家是维护法律的最高主宰——即使只在一个方面如此——，而面对外邦时也是如此——至少在这方面，一切权利都从它出发，必须由它来裁夺，而不是偶然、不是文书和其他法权名分。

en: [...] [it] can, whereby the freedom of the judicial power is endangered.

But the administration of justice steps entirely out of its nature if state power is to become its object, because thereby it, which is essentially only a part of the state, would thereby be set above the whole, in whose arbitrariness it stands to submit itself to the part or not, and the whole is there where the power is; for the power is the union of the individuals.

So long as the powers are not so organized that on the side of what is called administration of justice there is at the same time also the power, this administration of justice is something purely theoretical, and it can pass into execution neither with regard to lesser disputed relations of the estates among one another through the actual imperial courts, nor with regard to the more significant ones and those relating to the obligations toward the whole, through the imperial diet.
To resolve the contradiction that lies in this, that state power is to be regarded and treated as private property, centuries have exerted themselves in vain.

The beautiful theory that occurring disputes should be decided not by the violence of arms, for violence can indeed not decide about right, but by judgment and right — to it practice has become unfaithful and has followed nature, and the relations of the more powerful estates of the Empire among one another and to the Empire have been transferred, by the necessity of the matter, out of the sphere of right into the sphere of politics.
Great estates that are at the same time monarchs of other states are anyway in a different relation to one another and, with regard to war and peace, not under the law of the peace of the land.

Smaller estates are indeed not supposed to wage war against one another according to the same; but through the right of alliance with foreign powers they are placed, only by a detour, in precisely this relation, and as an ally of a foreign state, e.g. a bishop of Münster in the previous century conquered the imperial city of Münster and turned it into a country town.

Also, [things] of greater importance, the possession of lands etc., have through the electoral capitulation and otherwise been formally made into objects of politics; about such objects it is not to be decided by imperial courts and the supreme judicial power, but by amicable agreement of the estates among themselves, and if it cannot happen through amicable agreement, then it necessarily happens through war.
The Jülich-Berg succession affair [...]
zh: [...]能够……，从而使司法权力的自由受到危害。
但司法如果要以国家权力为对象，就完全走出了自己的本性，因为这样一来，它——本质上只是国家的一个部分——就被置于整体之上了，而整体要不要服从这个部分，全凭它的任意，并且整体在哪儿有权力就在哪儿；因为权力就是各个个人的结合。
只要各种权力还没有被组织成：在被称为司法的那一边同时也拥有权力，那么这种司法就纯粹是理论上的东西，它既不能在各个等级彼此之间较小的争执关系上通过真正的帝国法院得到执行，也不能在那些更重大的、涉及对整体所负义务的争执上通过帝国议会得到执行。
要解决这样一个矛盾——即国家权力竟应被看作并当作私有财产来对待——，几个世纪以来都是白费力气。
那种美好的理论说，发生的争执不应由武器的暴力来裁断——因为暴力根本不能裁断权利——，而应由判决和权利来裁断；实践却对它不忠，跟随了自然，而帝国中较强大的各等级彼此之间以及与帝国的关系，也由于事情本身的必然性，从权利的领域被挪进了政治的领域。
那些同时是别的国家君主的大等级，彼此之间本来就在另一种关系之中，并且在战争与和平方面不受国内和平法则的约束。
较小的等级按同一法则虽然不应互相开战；但他们凭借与外部势力结盟的权利，只是绕一个弯，就被置于恰恰这同一种关系之中，例如上个世纪有一位明斯特主教作为某个外邦的盟友，攻下了帝国城市明斯特，把它变成了一个地方城市。
此外，一些更重要的事情，比如对地方的占有等等，也通过选举投降书和其他方式被正式变成了政治的对象；这类事情不应由帝国法院和最高司法权力来裁断，而应由各等级彼此之间的友好协商来裁断，如果通过友好协商办不成，那就必然要通过战争来办。
于利希—贝格继承事件 [...]

en: The legal institution is thus so constituted that, when right is spoken in matters of state law, it cannot be executed, except when the interests concern an impotent estate; but if this is not the case, and usually it comes to no legal judgment at all, the decision is made according to power and political relations.
zh: 所以司法制度就是这样：在国法关系里作出权利判决时，判决执行不了，除非所涉及的利益属于一个无力的等级；但如果不是这种情况——而且通常根本不会作出权利判决——那就按权力和政治关系来决定。

en: That state power exists is the demand, and it is not to be a mere thing of thought, but is to have execution and reality; and that this execution is a real execution, legal procedure is instituted against him who refuses submission; but the realization of this legal procedure is a thing of thought.
zh: 国家权力存在，这是要求，而且它不该只是一个思想之物，而该有执行和实在性；为了使这种执行成为现实的执行，对那个拒绝臣服的人规定了法律程序；但这种法律程序的实现却是一个思想之物。

18.en: Chapter. Lawfulness, that the exercise of the state laws does not come about
18.zh: 章 合法性，即国家法律的施行无法实现

en: It has been set forth in the preceding chapter that the state remains a state of thought because legal procedure has no execution; the force of legal procedure is hindered by power, and one would first have to judge of this that this hindrance is something unlawful, and indeed, because it concerns the existence of the state itself and the state power, the greatest crime, high treason and crime of injured majesty.

But one would err if one wanted to judge merely according to the concept; for the resistance to the resolutions of the state power has itself been raised into the form of right; it is done legally when the state is hindered from being a state, since the power which can resist it is lawful.
zh: 上一章已经说明，国家之所以还是一个思想中的国家，是因为法律程序没有执行；法律程序的力量被权力阻挡，而人们首先必须对此作出判断：这种阻挡是不法的，而且因为它涉及国家自身的存在和国家权力，所以是最大的罪行，是叛国和侵害君主的罪行。
但若只按概念来判断，人们就会弄错；因为对国家权力决议的抵抗本身已被提升为权利的形式；当国家被阻止成为国家时，这样做是合法的，因为能够抵抗它的那种权力是合法的。

en: That the state is only a thing of thought lies in this, that as a state it has no power, but that power is in the hands of individuals, and to acknowledge power mutually through electoral capitulation, peace treaties and thus to make it lawful, this has been the general tendency of the political character of Germany ever since the relation of the state to individuals became an object of contracts.

In the working-out from crudeness to culture it depended on which of the two, the universal, the state, or the individuals, would gain the upper hand; in most European countries the state has completely carried off the victory, in some in an incomplete manner, in none so imperfectly as in Germany with regard to the pretension to be a state.
The condition of barbarism consists namely in this, that a multitude is a people without at the same time being a state, that the state and the individuals exist in opposition and in a separation.
The regent is as a personality state power, and the rescue against his personality is again only opposition of personality.

In a cultured state there stand between the personality of the monarch and the individuals the laws or the universality; the individual act of the monarch concerns all, burdens or injures all or benefits all.
But that the monarch is at the same time state power, or that he has the highest power, that there is a state at all, is synonymous.

The contradiction that the state is the highest power and that the individuals are not crushed by it is resolved by the power of the laws; it is the unbelief in the power of the laws that stems from the lack of wisdom, which wavers between the necessity of giving the state the highest power and the fear that the individual will be crushed by it.

On the solution of this task rests all the wisdom of the organization of states; but the first thing is that there be a state, the first thing therefore that the power of the state be the highest; but immediately therein lies also that there are laws;
zh: 国家只是一个思想之物，这一点就在于：它作为国家没有权力，权力反而在个人手里，而通过选举投降书、和平条约来互相承认权力，从而使它成为合法的，自从国家与个人的关系成为契约的对象以来，这一直是德意志政治性格的普遍倾向。
在从粗野向文化迈进的过程中，关键在于两者中哪一个占上风，是普遍者、国家，还是个人；在欧洲大多数国家里，国家完全取得了胜利，在一些国家里是以不完整的方式，而在自命为一个国家这一点上，没有哪个国家像德意志这样不完整。
野蛮状态就在于：一群人是一个民族，却不同时是一个国家，国家和个人处在对立和分离之中。
摄政者作为一个人格就是国家权力，而针对其人格的自救又只是人格的对立。
在一个有教养的国家里，在君主的人格和个人之间站着法律或普遍性；君主的个别行为涉及所有人，给所有人加负担或伤害所有人，或者有益于所有人。
但君主同时就是国家权力，或者说他拥有最高的权力，与根本存在着一个国家，是同一回事。
国家是最高的权力，而个人并没有被它压碎——这个矛盾由法律的权力来解决；对法律权力的不信任才出自智慧的缺乏，这种缺乏在必须给国家最高权力和害怕个人被它压碎之间摇摆。
国家的组织的一切智慧都建立在对这一任务的解决上；但首要的是有一个国家，所以首要的是国家的权力是最高的；而直接在这里面也就包含着：有法律存在；

en: 2. With regard to the general union of states, religion is an important determining ground of the relation of the individual provinces of Germany to the whole; the separation of religion has probably contributed most to tearing apart this union of states and to making this tearing apart lawful, because the princes could find no better help for it than in the conscience of their subjects, or also because the times into which these religious separations fell were too clumsy to separate the church from the state and, despite the separation of faith, to preserve the state.
zh: 2. 就普遍的邦国联合体而言，宗教是德意志各单个邦与整体之关系的一个重要规定根据；宗教的分离大概最有助于撕碎这个邦国联合体，并使这种撕碎成为合法的，因为诸侯们为此找不到比其臣民的良心更好的帮助，或者也因为这些宗教分裂所落入的时代太笨拙，无法把教会与国家分开，并且在信仰分裂的情况下仍把国家保存下来。

en: That the religion of every land, of every imperial city is determined by law, the one purely evangelical, the other purely catholic, a third parity (how, if a land so greatly violated the Peace of Westphalia and became purely protestant out of purely catholic or purely catholic out of purely protestant, or a pure one out of a parity one?), that the votes in the imperial diet, in the imperial chamber court, imperial court council are determined, that appointments, envoy posts depend on it, that a great part of the catholic votes, the archiepiscopal and episcopal ones, are most intimately interwoven with the church system - these are lawful determinations of state relations according to religion, sanctified by the most solemn treaties and fundamental laws of the empire; but they are small abuses compared with the lawful, so famous itio in partes - the right of the one or the other religious part not to submit to the majority; if this right were restricted to religious matters, it goes without saying that this separation would have to be lawful, and it would also be quite harmless for the state, because it would concern only objects which are nothing to do with it.

But as it is, it has many sides which utterly destroy relations in a state; in the first place a mass of things is connected with religion, property, privileges of every kind, which through the connection with religion become church matters, the matter of a state of its own.

Whole states of Germany, a monstrous mass of goods in catholic and protestant states, marriage matters, which by the protestants' own admission, as far as theirs are concerned, are purely things capable of a contract, whose relation necessarily are objects of contracts and require a government, are withdrawn from the general state.

But still more, and this is strong, the activity of the state can be completely paralyzed in every general state affair which has quite and altogether no reference to religion; about war and peace, taxes and the little that is left to the state, those of one religion can assemble and hinder everything that should be decided by the majority.
Brandenburg does not pay the increased chamber targets, for this reason.
It is going too far when one, as some do, places this right in complete parallel with the insurrection right which is sanctioned in the Robespierre constitution.

The difference is that the German Reich in its various parts has governments independent of the whole; but if the state and the governments and the laws rested on the resolutions of the Emperor and the Empire, then the two would be put on the same footing.
zh: 每个邦、每个帝国城市的宗教都由法律规定，一个是纯福音派的，另一个是纯天主教的，第三个是均分制的（如果某个邦如此严重地违反《威斯特伐利亚和约》，从纯天主教变成纯新教，或从纯新教变成纯天主教，或从均分制的变成一个纯粹的，那该怎么办呢？），帝国议会、帝国枢密法院、帝国宫廷枢密院中的票数是确定的，任职、使节职位都取决于此，天主教票数中很大一部分，即大主教和主教的票数，与教会体系最紧密地交织在一起，——这些都是按宗教对国法关系所作的法律规定，由帝国最隆重的条约和根本法神圣化；但与那合法的、如此著名的 itio in partes 相比，这些只是小小的弊病，——即这一方或那一方宗教派别不服从多数的权利；如果这项权利被限制在宗教事务上，那么不言而喻，这种分离必定是合法的，而且它对国家也完全无害，因为它只会涉及与国家毫不相干的对象。
但实际情形是，它有许多方面会完全摧毁一个国家里的各种关系；首先，一大堆东西与宗教相关联，财产、各种权利，它们通过与宗教的关联变成教会事务，变成一个自己的国家的事务。
德意志的整个整个邦，天主教和新教国家中一大批财产，婚姻事务，——按新教徒自己承认的，就他们自己的婚姻事务而言，纯粹是能够订立契约的事情，其关系必然成为契约的对象并需要一个政府，——都被从普遍的国家中抽走了。
但更甚的是，而且这一点很厉害：在每一件完全与宗教毫无关联的普遍国家事务上，国家的活动都能被完全阻止；关于战争与和平、税收以及剩下给国家的那一点点东西，属于一个宗教的人可以聚在一起，阻碍所有本应由多数决定的事情。
勃兰登堡不支付提高后的帝国税，就是这个缘故。
如果有人像某些人那样，把这项权利与罗伯斯庇尔宪法里得到认可的起义权完全并列起来，那就走得太远了。
区别在于，德意志帝国在其各个部分中有独立于整体的政府；但如果国家和各政府及法律都建立在皇帝与帝国的决议之上，那么两者就可以等同了。

en: c) In that religion has torn the state apart, it has however helped to promote another separation, at least some parts of it, and thereby given force to some principles which are necessary conditions of the existence of a state.

In that the protestants wove their religious rights into the state, in that they made the most important parts of state law dependent on religion, two religions have thereby nevertheless been woven into the state, and thereby an independence of the state from the church has not at all been established in part, but has nevertheless been prepared; there always lies in it the principle, which indeed in practice has itself been acted quite contrary to, that, despite different religions, a state is possible.
zh: c) 宗教既然把国家撕碎了，它却也帮助促成了另一种分离，至少促成其中某些部分，并因此使一些原则有了力量，而这些原则是国家存在的必要条件。
新教徒把他们的宗教权利织进国家，把国法最重要的部分弄成依赖于宗教的，这样一来毕竟有两种宗教被织进了国家，国家的独立于教会也因此部分地根本没有被确立，却被准备出来了；这里面总是含有这样一条原则，尽管实际行动本身完全违背了它：尽管宗教不同，一个国家是可能的。

en: But much more important for the state is another separation, through which the concept of the state as a universality has been elevated.

The deliberations and resolutions of the imperial diet rested, especially when the princes still appeared in person, on the person of the prince, they voted and resolved as princes of their land; princes of different lands had after all only one vote; their person and their land did not appear separated in this, or the concept of distinguishing them as princely persons and as representatives of their land did not become visible.
But in the so important affair of religion this difference soon came to the fore; how namely, if the prince and his land were of different religions?
For his person the catholic prince of a protestant land was on the side of the catholics; but his land, which was protestant?
Here the feeling of the difference awoke also with regard to the general union of states.
To be sure, as a state power he should have been on neither side or on both sides.

But that was not possible for those times; the prince of Palatinate-Neuburg, whose land was evangelical and who became catholic in the 17th century, was counted with the catholic votes at the imperial diet as well as with regard to the imperial chamber court.

On the other hand, at the end of that same century, at the change of religion of the Elector of Saxony, his vote remained evangelical, as likewise happened in the following period at other changes of religion, in Württemberg and Hesse.

Now although even before this only princes who had land and people to govern had seat and vote at the imperial diet, so that the land seemed inseparable from the concept of an estate at the imperial diet, this distinction first became legal now also with regard to the general German state; and the separation in this respect was found easier and less strained where the separation of the interest of the prince and of his subjects within a land had already come about and was previously established constitutionally through provincial estates.

The Palatinate, which had no provincial estates, went over to the catholic part without resistance, and the struggle of the Palatines with their catholic princes over religious grievances has continued down to the present times; in Württemberg and Hesse, lands in which the separation through provincial estates had already taken place, the religion of the land was asserted with regard to its relation to the German Reich; this relation thus remained no longer personal, the person of the prince, and indeed the most personal thing about him, his religion, has become indifferent, and he appears purely as a representative. - This occasion for becoming attentive to this difference was then extended from religion to other differences; namely different lands which came under one prince have different votes, so the unity of the person of the regent does not come into consideration, but only his quality as representative.
Of a respect which this representation has through its kind, namely to unite in itself a power which is capable of resisting the state, there is otherwise spoken.
zh: 但对国家重要得多的，是另一种分离，通过它，国家作为普遍性的概念被提高了。
帝国议会的商议和决议，尤其在诸侯还亲自出席的时候，都建立在诸侯这个人身上，他们作为自己邦的诸侯投票和决议；不同邦的诸侯毕竟只有一票；在这里他们的人身和他们的邦并不显得是分开的，或者说，把他们作为诸侯人身和作为其邦的代表加以区别这一概念，并没有变得可见。
但在宗教这件如此重要的事情上，这种区别很快就显露出来了；也就是说，如果诸侯和他的邦宗教不同，那该怎么办呢？
就他本人来说，一个新教邦的天主教诸侯站在天主教徒一边；但他的邦，那个新教的邦呢？
在这里，区别的感觉也就普遍邦国联合体这一方面被唤醒了。
当然，他作为国家权力本应不站在任何一边，或者站在两边。
但那对当时那些时代是不可能的；普法尔茨-诺伊堡的侯爵，他的邦是福音派的，而他本人在17世纪成了天主教徒，在帝国议会以及在帝国枢密法院方面都被算作天主教票。
相反，在同一世纪末，萨克森选帝侯改宗时，他的票仍是福音派的，就像在随后时期其他改宗时也同样如此，在符腾堡和黑森。
尽管此前也只有须治理土地和人民的诸侯才在帝国议会有席位和票，所以土地似乎与帝国议会中一个等级的概念不可分离，但这一区分现在才也在普遍的德意志国家方面成为合法的；而这种方面上的分离，在一个邦之内诸侯与其臣民利益的分离已经发生、并且此前已通过地方等级按宪法确定下来的地方，就显得更容易、更自然。

普法尔茨没有地方等级，便毫无抵抗地转到天主教一方，而普法尔茨人与其天主教诸侯为宗教疾苦所作的斗争一直持续到今天；在符腾堡和黑森，即分离已由地方等级完成的那些邦，邦的宗教在其与德意志帝国的关系方面被主张出来；于是这种关系不再是人身性的，诸侯的人身，而且是其最人身性的东西即宗教，已变得无关紧要，他纯粹作为代表出现。——这个使人注意到这一区别的机缘，随后又从宗教扩展到其他差异上；也就是说，归于一个诸侯之下的不同邦有不同的票，所以摄政者人身的统一不被考虑，只有他作为代表的属性才算数。
至于这种代表制凭其方式所具有的一个方面，即把一种能够抵抗国家的权力联合在自身之内，这将在别处谈到。

en: C. The feudal constitution is destroyed in Germany by the independence of the vassals from the feudal lord.

The principle of the feudal constitution, that descent from a princely, comital, noble line [gives] a right to lordship over land and people, has for the most part been abolished by the introduction of primogeniture in the princely houses, and one of its most important consequences, the harmlessness of the vassals for the whole, has been lost; in its place there has stepped the greater power of the territories, insofar as it is bound up with the person of the prince, but at the same time does not so much leave the importance of the same to his character and his individuality, but rather raises it above the universal state power.
zh: C. 在德意志，封建采邑制已经被封臣对采邑领主的独立摧毁了。
封建采邑制的原则，即出身于诸侯、伯爵、贵族世家[就]拥有对土地和人民的统治的权利，由于各诸侯家族引入长子继承权而大体上已经被废除，而它最重要的后果之一，即封臣对整体无害，也随之失去了；取而代之的是各邦更大的权力，这种权力在于它与诸侯本人相联系，但同时并不把它的重要性交给他的性格和他的个体性，而是把它抬高到普遍的国家权力之上。

en: Through the independence of the power of an estate from the whole of the state, and through the relation of the estates to one another as states, the condition of Germany in the relation of the estates to one another has, as regards principle, gone back to the condition before the Land Peace; in that condition the estates could act against one another as sovereigns, wage war on one another, make alliances with one another, yet over them all there still prevailed a superior power, which now no longer takes place at all.
By contrast, another difference has entered in, which relates not so much to principles and right as to prudence.
zh: 由于一个等级的权力独立于国家的整体，也由于各等级彼此像国家一样相互对待，德意志在各等级相互关系的状况上按原则来说已经退回到邦国和平之前的状态；在那种状态里，各等级还能作为主权者彼此行事、互相开战、彼此结盟，但在它们全体之上还存在着一种压倒性的力量，而这种力量如今根本不再有了。
与此相对，出现了另一种差别，它与其说关系到原则和权利，不如说关系到精明。

en: For in the course of time the power of the states by which the smaller ones are surrounded has completely changed; the great territories have come to inner stability and have become states; among all European states there has thereby arisen such a connection that they, inwardly calmed, have leisure to turn their attention outward and to make their weight felt with others.
zh: 因为随着时间推移，那些包围着较小邦国的国家的力量已经完全变了，大的领地获得了内部的稳定并成了国家；由此在所有欧洲国家之间产生了这样一种联系，使它们在内心里安定下来之后有余暇把注意力转向外部，并在别人那里发挥自己的分量。

en: A union of imperial cities in southern Germany waged fortunate wars against the allied princes and barons of the same; the fleets of the Hanse were terrible to the northern kingdoms, they ruled the northern seas.

A union of the nobility with Sickingen conquered electoral principalities; Maurice of Saxony made the mighty Charles, emperor of Germany, lord of Italy, Spain, Hungary, the Netherlands, Mexico and Peru, tremble and forced him to peace, and that without the help of a foreign power, at a time when Charles was not otherwise occupied or in distress.
zh: 德意志南部一些帝国城市结成的联盟，对那里结盟的诸侯和男爵打过几场得手的战争；汉萨同盟的舰队让北方的王国感到可怕，它们控制着北方诸海。
贵族与济金根结成联盟，攻下了几个选侯国；萨克森的莫里茨让强大的查理——德意志的皇帝，意大利、西班牙、匈牙利、尼德兰、墨西哥和秘鲁的主人——发抖，并逼他讲和，而且这没有借助任何外来力量，是在查理并没有别的事情缠身或没有陷入困境的时候。

en: These times are past; no German imperial estate will want to appeal to the example of Venice, which later held its own against the League of Cambrai, or even of the Marquis de Brandebour and his resistance to the union of the greatest powers of Europe, or to rely on it.

The relation of power, even if the German estates have also become more powerful, has completely changed; against the state colossi they have become pygmies; from their power as individuals they cannot hope for their preservation, nor from their union; politics has in itself become too calculating for each individual not to be able to see in his combination either loss or at least a smaller advantage than another has, and the jealousy of this lagging behind must separate them.

Besides, however, it is precisely in a union that the German estates would have to give up that which they aim at or for which they fought; namely, they would have to subject themselves to a universal, to laws of the union, to set a power of the whole over themselves, and it is precisely this against which they strive.
zh: 那样的时代已经过去了；威尼斯后来顶住了康布雷同盟，还有勃兰登堡侯爵以及他对欧洲最强大几个国家的联合的抵抗，这样的例子，德意志的任何一个帝国等级都不会想去引证，也不会想依靠。
力量的关系已经完全变了，即使德意志各等级也变得更加强大；面对那些国家庞然大物，他们成了侏儒；他们不能指望靠他们作为单个人的力量来保全自己，也不能指望靠他们的结合来保全自己；政治本身已经变得太会算计，以致于每个人在自己的联合里都难免会看到，要么是损失，要么至少是比别人更少的好处，而这种落在后面的嫉妒心必然把他们分开。
可是除此之外，德意志各等级恰恰在一种结合里必须放弃他们所要达到的、或者他们为之斗争的东西；也就是说，他们必须服从一个普遍者、服从结合的法律，在自己之上设定一种整体的权力，而恰恰这就是他们竭力反对的东西。

en: The very nature of the matter already lifts territorial lordship, sovereignty, above the sphere of the courts.

The Peace of Westphalia has expressly accepted foreign powers as guarantors; practice has decided all important cases through negotiations or war; imperial laws have determined that such cases should be brought before emperor and empire, thus should be decided by the legislative, not by the judicial power; the emperor has reserved them to himself in his supreme judicial power, that is, rather, [reserved them] to himself as the supreme member of the state power, as representative of the state.

The decision must be taken with the consent of the powerful estate, otherwise it resists through the masses, or, like the weak one, has the right to call upon foreign powers as guarantors for support of that which it calls its right, and according to the weight or the fortune of arms and interest which they have for themselves in the matter, the dispute decides itself; without a trace of judicial proceeding.182) What before the Land Peace the fist and wild boldness, personal strength decided, is now decided by politics, that is, by the support of the more powerful and the power of those who for the moment have the same interest, and by favourable circumstances, that is, the momentary incapacity of those who [have] an opposite interest.

In place of the sudden striking out has stepped calculation of consequences; in place of personal courage, calculation of the forces of the opponent; in place of the fist, calculation of the powers in general that would be for or against an interest.

The difference is like when boys or old men play chess; or like between a tournament fight and the campaigns of a Fabius; there with an equal blow for blow, even with danger to life; everything for the thanks of the lady and for honour; here deliberate and artful, years-long observation and evasion of the opponent, everything for possession.
Neither over the feuds nor over the present political wrestling do judges sit in judgment.
zh: 事情的本性本身就已经把邦君统治、把主权抬到了法庭的范围之上。
《威斯特伐利亚和约》明确把外国列强接纳为保证人；实际做法把一切重要的事例都通过谈判或战争来裁定；帝国法律曾经规定，这类事例应当提交皇帝和帝国，也就是应当由立法的权力、而不是由司法的权力来裁定；而皇帝却把它们保留给自己，凭自己最高的司法权力保留给自己，也就是说，毋宁是保留给作为国家权力最高成员、作为国家代表的自己。

决定必须得到强大等级的同意才能作出，否则它就通过民众来对抗，或者像弱小的等级一样，有权把外国列强作为保证人召来，以支援他称之为自己的权利的东西，而争端就按它们在其中为自己取得的份量、或者按战运和利益来决定；全无司法审理的影子。182) 在邦国和平之前由拳头、由蛮勇、由个人的力量来决定的事情，如今是由政治，也就是由更强大者的支持、由那些一时有着相同利益的人的力量，以及由有利的形势，也就是由那些[有着]相反利益的人一时无力，来决定。
取代突然动手的，是对后果的计算；取代个人勇气的，是对对手力量的计算；取代拳头的，是对那些可能赞成或反对某一利益的各股力量的计算。
这种差别就像小孩子或老头下棋；或者像一场马上比武和费边的战役之间的差别；那边是势均力敌地你来我往，甚至冒着生命危险；一切都是为了贵妇人的青睐和荣誉；这边是审慎而巧妙地对敌人经年累月的观察和回避，一切都是为了占有。
无论是私战，还是当今的政治角力，都没有法官开庭审理。

en: The Peace of Westphalia is one of the most important fundamental laws concerning the possession of every estate; what power is it that maintains it and the remaining imperial laws and peace settlements.
zh: 《威斯特伐利亚和约》是关于每个等级的占有的最重要的根本法律之一；究竟哪一种力量在维持它以及其余的帝国法律和各个和约呢。

en: In the Peace of Westphalia itself it is granted to all who would be injured in the rights laid down by it to put themselves into possession by self-help; in order to be able to do this, one must have power enough for it, — the attack or the self-help becomes a matter of calculation and of politics.
zh: 在《威斯特伐利亚和约》本身里，就已经准许所有在它规定的权利上会受到侵害的人，通过自助来取得占有；而要做到这一点，人就必须有足够的力量，——攻击或自助于是成了计算和政治的事情。

zh: c) 在德意志不存在最高的权力

zh: [邦君主权与帝国权力]

en: ... to go into their origin and legal grounding; such investigations usually have the purpose of finding that result about which interest has already decided.
zh: ……去追究它们的起源和法理根据；这类考察通常的目的，就是找出那个利益早已决定了的结论。

en: Territorial sovereignty, the pride of the German estates, the pride of their subjects, of belonging to a particular state, is with a view to the whole the principle by which it is torn apart, one is incompatible with the other; but it has so many alluring charms, it was so much supported by the character of the people, that every estate overlooked that this separation is the pit he digs for himself, that the more progress he makes in his striving to isolate himself, he loses in strength, that every gain is an enlargement of the danger. - The striving of the imperial estates offers the spectacle of a crowd that throws itself onto a frozen river, from whose ice each strives to tear off as much as possible for himself, unmindful that the more he enriches himself, the more he hastens his own and everyone's downfall.

If this drive to isolate is the only moving principle in the German Empire, then Germany finds itself in an unstoppable decline into the abyss of its dissolution, and a warning against it would indeed show zeal, but at the same time the folly of an unnecessary effort.
Should Germany's course not still find itself at the crossroads between Italy's fate and the union into one state?
It is chiefly two circumstances that give hope for the latter, two circumstances that can be regarded as a tendency against its dissolving principle.
zh: 邦君主权，德意志各等级的骄傲，他们的臣民的骄傲——即属于一个特别的国家，就整体来看就是那个把整体撕碎的原则，一方与另一方不能相容；可是它有那么多诱人的魅力，它得到民族性格那么大的支持，以至于每个等级都看不见：这种分离正是他自己给自己挖的坑，他在把自己孤立起来的努力中越是前进，就越失去力量，每一次所得都是危险的扩大。——帝国各等级的努力提供了一幅景象：一群人扑向一条冻结的河流，人人都想从它的冰上尽可能多地为自个儿掰下一块，却不想想他越是发财，就越是加速自己和所有人的毁灭。
如果这种孤立化的冲动是德意志帝国唯一的推动原则，那么德意志就处在不可阻挡地坠入自身瓦解的深渊之中，而对此发出警告，固然会显出热忱，同时也会显出做一件不必要之事的愚蠢。
德意志的行程难道不还处在意大利的命运与结合为一个国家这两者之间的岔路口上吗？
主要是两种情况给了后者的希望，这两种情况可以看作对抗它那瓦解原则的一种趋向。

en: Formerly, on the one side, the territorial sovereignty183) of the prince or of the city flowed together with freedom, especially also religious freedom, on the other side the union of the empire...
zh: 从前，一方面，邦君或城市的邦君主权183)与自由、尤其也与宗教自由合流，另一方面，帝国的结合……

en: [war force]
zh: [战争武力]

en: enemy of the empire, the third a neutrality treaty etc. and leaves without help the attacked fellow estate to the devastating superiority of the enemy and to his own weakness; an estate votes in the imperial diet that its alliances do not permit it to take part in the raising of an imperial army and the payment of the Roman months for the war; are there for an imperial estate holier alliances than its feudal duties toward the empire?
But no!
The imperial laws give the imperial estate the right to conclude alliances with foreign powers; it therefore has legally the choice between union with the empire and foreign powers.

The empire will not give itself a constitution by which it would be strong enough to protect its members against foreign enemies; the estate that is in danger is thereby put into the state of nature and is entitled and obligated to provide for itself as well as it can; it would be highly unnatural to demand that one rely on a protection that is known to the world not to be able to protect and is legally and rightfully refused by the right to conclude alliances, that is, by not supplying the protecting contingents; it becomes necessary for the weaker to place itself under the protection of foreign powers, which is all the more feasible because these foreign powers are at the same time fellow estates of the empire, but according to their interest and independence are only called fellow estates.

This granted protection is, because it is sought only temporarily, no protection-lordship; nor for that reason, because in more recent times such a name is avoided and each is gladly left the title of an independent state, as France too in its treaties with the Cisalpine and Batavian Republic did not call itself protector, although it places armies in these states as garrisons and for that draws annual sums, which are also not called protection money, and the first paragraph of such an agreement always contains the recognition of the independence of the other state.
zh: 帝国的敌人，第三个一份中立条约等等，并且把受到攻击的同等级伙伴丢下不管，任其面对敌人毁灭性的优势和他自己的软弱；一个等级在帝国议会上投票说，他的结盟不允许他参加组建一支帝国军队和支付战争用的罗马月捐；对一个帝国等级来说，还有比他对帝国的封建义务更神圣的结盟吗？
可是不！
帝国法律给帝国等级以同外国势力缔结同盟的权利；所以他依法可以在与帝国结合和与外国势力结合之间作选择。

帝国不愿给自己一部宪法，使自己强大到足以保护自己的成员抵御外来敌人；因此，处在危险中的等级就被置入自然状态，并且有权也有义务尽可能自己照顾自己；要求人信赖一种全世界都知道保护不了、而且在法律上和法理上又通过缔结同盟的权利、也就是通过不提供那些提供保护的分遣队而被拒绝的保护，那是极不自然的；较弱的等级必然要托庇于外国势力，而这之所以更容易行得通，是因为这些外国势力同时是帝国的同等级伙伴，但按它们的利益和独立来说只叫作同等级伙伴。
这种被给予的保护，因为只是暂时寻求的，不是保护权；也不是因为这个理由，因为在较新的时代这样的名号被避开，人们乐于让每个国家保留独立国家的头衔，就像法国在同内阿尔卑斯共和国和巴达维亚共和国的条约里也没有自称保护者，尽管它把军队当作驻军放进这些国家，并为此收取年款，而这些款项也不叫保护费，并且这种协定的第一条总是包含对另一国家独立的承认。

en: This warlike weakness of the German Empire is, as is clear from what has been said, not a consequence of cowardice on the part of its inhabitants.

The Germans are not an unwarlike nation, nor unfamiliar with the skills that in more recent times contribute as much to victory as bravery; rather, even in this unhappy war the imperial contingents have on various occasions proved themselves [through] the greatest proofs of courage and bravery, worthy of their forefathers.
But there is no blessing in it.
Through the powerlessness and weakness of the whole, because not all estates work together toward the whole, all efforts and sacrifices of individual men and corps are lost (Ehrenbreitstein).

One could bring under this point of view everything that has happened in this war, how the consequences of individual operations, which were expedient in themselves, were again destroyed [by the fact] that the empire did not support those consequences ...
zh: 德意志帝国这种战争上的软弱，从上面所说的可以看清，并不是它的居民怯懦的结果。
德意志人并不是一个不好战的民族，也不是不熟悉那些在较新时代与勇敢同样有助于取胜的本领；相反，甚至在这场不幸的战争中，帝国分遣队也在各种场合以最大的勇气和勇敢的证明表明自己配得上他们的祖先。
可是其中没有福气。
由于整体的无力和软弱，因为并非所有等级都共同为整体出力，个别人和军团的全部努力与牺牲都白费了（埃伦布赖特施泰因）。
从这个观点可以看待这场战争中发生的一切，看待那些本身合乎目的的各次作战的后果，如何又因为帝国不支持那些后果而被毁掉……

en: [finances]
zh: [财政]

en: Since the German constitution is an old heirloom, the German state has had no finances to inherit, and in more recent times one did not let it get to the point of making arrangements about them.
zh: 因为德意志的宪法是一件古老的遗产，所以德意志国家没有财政可继承，而在较近的时代，人们也不让它走到为此作出安排的地步。

en: In the pure feudal constitution the supreme feudal lord has domains for defraying those costs that the (conduct of) overlordship causes him; the expense for war every vassal has to defray himself; state revenues are quite superfluous.

In the most recent times one has seen the other extreme of a lack of finances, namely that every expenditure that a state office, down to the village magistrate's office (juge de paix) and still further down [requires], flows as a contribution first to the supreme state power and as expenditure from this back into the smallest branches of the public service.

The supreme direction of the state over the finances has become a mania, to tie everything that is required for the service of however insignificant a state power, in however small a scope, to the supreme power, to let no village provide for the pay of its bailiff.

This care of the state is superfluous and therefore becomes harmful; if a power does not let a community do something that it can and will perform itself, that stands in no relation to the whole, then this superfluous interference appears as a tyranny.
zh: 在纯粹的封建采邑制中，最高的封君拥有领地，用来支付（行使）宗主权给他造成的那些开销；战争的花费每个封臣都得自己承担；国家收入则完全是多余的。
在最近的时代，人们看到了没有财政的另一个极端，就是每一笔支出，哪怕是一个国家公职、直到村法官职位（juge de paix）乃至更低者[所需要的]，都先作为捐税流到最高国家权力那里，再作为支出从它那里流回到公共事业最细小的枝节中去。
国家对财政的最高管理已经变成一种癖好：把为任何一个再微不足道的国家权力、在再小的范围里所需要的一切，都挂到最高权力上去，不让一个村庄自己负担它那个差役的薪水。
国家这种操心是多余的，因此也变得有害；如果一个权力不让一个共同体去做某件它自己能够也愿意做、并且与整体毫无关系的事，那么这种多余的插手就显得是一种专制。

en: In the German Empire not only the immediate estates but also the country towns in principalities, even villages, mostly provide [for] the finances that concern themselves, provide for the pay of their magistrates, courts, etc., all under supreme supervision; and because the purpose of those expenditures is so limited and they anyway rest on old custom and are small, the state need not mix into them in any other way at all, only into what concerns the general; if they hindered this general, were too great and made the contribution for the state harder, then the state would have to look into it.
zh: 在德意志帝国，不只是直属等级，连各侯国里的内地城市、甚至村庄，也大多自己[为]与自身相关的财政操心，自己负担它们的长官、法院等等的薪水，这一切都在最高监督之下；而且因为那些支出的目的如此有限，它们又本来就依据古老的习惯、数目也小，所以国家根本不必以别的方式插手其中，只须管那些与普遍的东西相关的事；要是它们妨碍了这种普遍的东西、变得太大、使给国家的那一份更难交，那么国家就得过问一下了。

en: The state is interested only in the expenditures and revenues that concern its power with regard to the maintenance of what the laws say and to security from foreign enemies.
zh: 国家感兴趣的只是那些支出和收入，它们涉及它的权力，就维持法律所说的事情以及不受外来敌人侵犯的安全而言。

en: As for that power for the maintenance of the laws, provision is made for it in the individual estates by the power of the same; the general state usually has nothing to do with it, every estate becomes master over its criminals; not always over insurrection, and then one is compelled to address the neighbouring estates, and these (as in the Liège affair) then gladly lend a helping hand; more powerful estates (at that time Prussia) may indeed not wish to content themselves with being mere executors of judicial verdicts, but believe themselves important and judicious enough to go to work at it according to their understanding and good intention, i.e. to play the matter out of the judicial into the political sphere; in the latter the matter might often be better ordered if the power is judicious and equitable, especially in the dispute between subjects and princes, where usually Iliacos intra [etc.] and the judge has to speak only according to cold right; but by this the whole standpoint of an executor, the whole principle of the constitution is shifted, the corner-stone of the state union shattered, or rather it is only revealed on such occasions that it has already been shattered beforehand.

In such cases, then, where the laws are to be exercised only against private persons, they can be exercised not by the state but by the estate; in case of need also with insurrections, because the interest of the princes in them is a common one.
zh: 至于那种维持法律的力量，在各个等级那里是由等级自身的力量来操办的；一般的国家通常与它不相干，每个等级都是自己那些罪犯的主人；但并不总是暴动的主人，这时人们就不得不去求助邻近的等级，而后者（像在列日事件中那样）便乐意伸出援手；更有力的等级（当时的普鲁士）自然不愿满足于只做司法判决的执行者，而是自以为足够重要、足够明达，要凭自己的见识和善良意图去办事，也就是说，把这件事从司法的领域挪到政治的领域里去；在后一个领域里，事情往往可能办得更好，只要那权力明达而公道，特别是在臣民与君主之间的争执中，那里通常是 Iliacos intra [etc.]，而法官只需按冷冰冰的权利说话；但这样一来，一个执行者的整个立场、宪法的整个原则就被挪动了，国家联合的支柱就被砸碎了，或者不如说，这种场合只是暴露出它早已被砸碎了。
所以，在那些法律只应当用来对付私人的场合，法律不能由国家、而只能由等级来执行；必要时在暴动中也是如此，因为各君主在其中的利益是共同的。

en: It is quite otherwise when the pronouncements of the laws are to be applied against estates; in this respect no sufficient state power is organized; on the contrary, the laws are so constituted that the laws cannot be applied; an insignificant estate must indeed crawl to the cross before a significant one, and that even in the case when not the laws but only the claims of the powerful have spoken; but where would be the state power that applies the laws against the powerful estate, the executive power that would put into actuality against a powerful man the rights of the weaker recognized by the judge?
zh: 如果法律的判决要用来对付各个等级，情形就完全不同了；在这方面并没有组织起足够的国家权力；相反，法律本身就是这样的性质，以致法律无法执行；一个无足轻重的等级面对一个重要的等级，当然只好卑躬屈膝，而且即使在说话的不是法律、只是强者的要求时，恐怕也是如此；可是，那个能对强大的等级执行法律的国家权力、那个能对强者把法官所确认的弱者的权利变成现实的执行权，又在哪里呢？

en: Execution ordinance.
zh: 执行条例。

en: What are the proposals for remedying these evils; for executing a prince who has over 200,000 men under his command?
zh: 补救这些祸害的建议是怎样的呢；怎样对一个手下有二十万以上兵力听他号令的君主实行强制执行呢？

en: Through the fact that the contingents are paid and fed by the estates themselves, the military system becomes entirely independent of a supreme power; if they only had to supply the men, the state would be independent of their negligence.
For it could already provide itself with men.
zh: 由于各分遣队由各等级自己出钱供养，军事制度就完全独立于一个最高权力之外了；要是它们只需提供人员，国家就不必受它们玩忽职守的拖累了。
因为它本来就弄得到人员。

en: But as things are, with regard to external defence a supreme power in Germany is a) neither according to right b) nor according to practice.
What the explicit right still left to the state, the famous, all-powerful principle of practice has abolished.
zh: 但这样一来，就对外防御而言，德意志的最高权力 a) 无论在权利上 b) 还是在实践上都不存在。
明确的权利还给国家留下的东西，那个著名的、无所不能的实践原则已经把它废除了。

en: C. One should have thought that the estates' own advantage would have moved them to hold Germany together as a state, since the existence of each single one rests entirely on the preservation of the whole as a united one.
But against the state there sets in the natural reaction of isolating oneself; as with contributions in general.

All wish and demand justice and government, all find contributions necessary, all demand [them], all pledge themselves to them; but each individual seeks to free himself from them as much as possible, he puts his contribution out of relation with the whole, considers his advantage separately from the general, and so with indirect imposts there is always an enormous falling-off against what they were supposed to bring in.

It has gone likewise in Germany with the state power; all estates demand protection from the German Empire, call for its help, demand that the German Empire protect them, acknowledge, especially the smaller ones, that without the whole they cannot hold themselves; but at the same time each seeks as much as possible from the state power [to free himself].
The estate's own advantage is the universal maxim, and in place of a constitution [there] has stepped politics.
Instead of the connection of the empire, of preserving it as the highest, one's own advantage.
First the power for that had to be procured.
This happened through alliances with foreign powers, these alliances have become legal.

Enlargement of one's own power - troops in themselves insignificant, except in Brandenburg - alliances among one another, still seems the best! - Only two things seemed possible, crudeness knew only, after the abolition of living together and acting in common, the relation of boundless domination of the state power, blind power and servile subjection.

The way out under common fixed laws unknown, but rather practice has triumphed over lawless rule, yet at the same time abolished all social connection, abolished tyranny through anarchy and made the latter legal.
Tyranny stands above anarchy, for in it the connection to a state still remains.
zh: C. 人们本该以为，各等级自身的利益会使它们把德意志作为一个国家保持在一起，因为每一个单个等级的存续完全取决于这个整体作为联合体的保存。
但针对国家，出现了自我隔离的自然反作用；就像一般的捐税一样。
所有人都希望并要求司法和治理，所有人都觉得捐税是必要的，所有人都要求[捐税]，所有人都为此许下承诺；但每一个单个的人都想尽量把自己从中解脱出来，他把自己那一份同整体脱开关系，把自己的好处同普遍的东西分开来看，于是在间接税上，总是同它们本该收进的数目相差得惊人。
在德意志，国家权力方面的情况也是如此；所有等级都向德意志帝国要求保护，呼求它的援助，要求德意志帝国保护它们，承认——尤其是那些较小的等级——没有整体它们就撑不住；但同时每一个又都想从国家权力那里尽量[脱身]。
等级自身的利益成了普遍的准则，而取代宪法的[是]政治。
取代帝国的整体联系、取代把它作为至高者来保持的，是自身的利益。
首先必须为此置办权力。
这是通过与外国势力的结盟做到的，这些结盟已经成了合法的东西。
扩大自己的权力——军队本身无足轻重，除了在勃兰登堡——彼此结盟，看来还是最好的办法！——看来只有两种可能，粗野在共同生活和共同行动被废除之后，只认得一种关系，即国家权力的无限统治、盲目暴力和奴性的屈服。
在共同的固定法律之下的出路不为人知，相反，实践战胜了无法无天的统治，但同时废除了所有社会联系，通过无政府状态废除了专制，并使后者变得合法。
专制高于无政府状态，因为在专制里毕竟还留着结合成一个国家的联系。

en: This separation from the highest state power happened with intention; but the consequence, anarchy and the robbing away of security, was not seen; clumsy.
zh: 这种同最高国家权力的脱离是有意为之的；但后果、无政府状态和安全被剥夺，却没有被看到；笨拙。

en: 185) Enlargement of the states through inheritances, especially their connections with foreign ones.

This circumstance is the deepest blow for the state; nothing has thereby been violated in the constitution, in the right; no foreign prince of those who still make up Germany (with the Italian fiefs it is another matter) has abolished the imperial union.
The German Empire has reserved all its rights to itself.
But the change is astonishing.

The relation of the power of the estates to the state system is utterly changed, and such a thing is called a revolution which, without a jot having needed to be changed in the state right, has stolen over the same and quite overturned it.
With England it is another matter, for the highest power of England and that of Hanover are not united, through the separation of the ministries.
The king could indeed unite them; he has the highest state power, to conclude war and peace, to make alliances, the administration of the treasury, command over the armies in both.
But only the administration of the treasury, not the granting.
Moreover, under George I the interest of both was united.
Had he been more fortunate, he would have snatched the role of Prussia to himself.
But England's interest is against France, hence with Austria.
Then it would have been against both and would not have maintained itself.
[The] role [of Prussia was] counter-power against the emperor and protection for lesser ones; thereby [it] put itself in the place of the imperial power in a part of Germany.
zh: 185）国家因继承而扩大，尤其是它们同外国的结合。
这一情形对国家是最深的一击；由此在宪法上、在权利上什么也没有受到侵害；那些还构成德意志的外国诸侯里（意大利的封地是另一回事），没有一个废除了帝国联合。
德意志帝国把自己的一切权利都保留了下来。
但变化是惊人的。
各等级的势力同国家体制的关系已经完全变了，这种事就叫一场革命：它在国家法上连一个字母都不需要改动，却悄悄溜了进来，把那套国家法整个推翻了。
同英国的情况则是另一回事，因为英国的最高权力和汉诺威的最高权力并没有合在一起，靠的是各部大臣的分开。
国王本来可以把它们合起来；他有最高的国家权力，缔结战争与和平、结成同盟、管理国库、统率两边的军队。
但只是管理国库，不是批准。
此外，在乔治一世治下，两者的利益是合在一起的。
他要是更走运一些，就会把普鲁士的角色抢到自己身上。
但英国的利害关系是针对法国的，因此是同奥地利站在一起。
那样它就会同时与两边为敌，也就维持不下去了。
〔普鲁士〕的角色〔是〕对抗皇帝的抗衡力量和对弱小者的保护；它由此在一个部分德意志里把自己放到了皇帝权力的位置上。

en: b) an aimless dissolution of the state seems to have been religion on the side of the peoples; the princes knew what they were doing, as shows through everywhere, the peoples honestly and uprightly for religion, and honestly and uprightly they thought of nothing else; national enmities produced at the same time through war and plunderings and mutual hostilities.
zh: b）一种没有意图的国家解体，从各民族这一方面看，似乎是宗教；诸侯们知道自己在做什么，这一点到处都透得出来，各民族则是老老实实、诚心诚意地为了宗教，而且老老实实、诚心诚意地没有去想别的；民族的敌意同时通过战争、抢掠和相互的敌对行为产生出来。

en: This separation in religion has become astonishingly important; in other countries nationality, the state, has after all prevailed over the enormous devastation, in Germany it was too clumsy to preserve this.
[There remained for] the emperor no other means than to make imperial princes, because he no longer gained votes.
Blindly or intentionally the state was made to go to ruin.
The emperor was only Catholic, himself a party, not the state as in France, as in the Austrian monarchy; and so then the Protestants too were only a party.
People did not speak of foreign influence; if they wanted to, they could.
zh: 这种宗教上的分裂变得重要得惊人；在别的国家，尽管有那场巨大的破坏，毕竟还是民族性、国家占了上风，在德意志则太笨拙，没能保住这一点。
〔留给〕皇帝的办法没有别的，只有册封帝国诸侯，因为他再也赢不到更多选票了。
人们或者是瞎了眼，或者是有意为之，让国家走向毁灭。
皇帝只是天主教徒，自己就是一个派别，而不是像在法国、在奥地利君主国那样就是国家；于是新教徒也同样只是一个派别。
人们并不谈外国的影响；他们要是想这样做，本来是做得到的。

en: Anarchy made legal through the Corpus Evangelicum, not merely religious matters, but also taxes and other things, likewise in the imperial chamber court and the imperial aulic council [there was] itio in partes.
Open use of religion.
Because political rights were bound to religion, both parties have thereby torn themselves away from the state power; for the separation of both parties has torn the bond apart.
zh: 无政府状态通过福音派团体（Corpus Evangelicum）变成了合法的，而且不只是宗教的事情，还有税收和别的事情，在帝国枢密法院和帝国宫廷议会里也一样是 itio in partes。
对宗教的公开利用。
因为政治权利被绑在了宗教上，两个派别就由此把自己从国家权力那里扯了出来；因为两个派别的分离把那条纽带扯断了。

en: That a state is now possible requires the separation of religion and politics; it is not for the highest power to have a power over religion, God forbid, but precisely no power over it, no rights in regard to it; only then is the highest power possible for the defense of the inner and the outer.
zh: 国家如今之所以可能，靠的是宗教和政治的分离；最高的权力并不是要有一种对宗教的权力——上帝保佑不要这样——，而恰恰是对它没有权力、在它面前没有权利；只有这样，最高的权力才可能用来防卫内部和外部。

en: D. Trust and obedience toward the highest power necessarily impossible with the separation of states in Germany.
That people to which the emperor belongs, be it now Austria or Bavaria or Brandenburg, its language and that of the [peoples] surrounding it is not even understood at all by others.

In this respect of trust, the difference of right is an astonishing source of estrangement; [as he who] is less oppressed with dues, the freer, lifts himself above the serf, the other [feels] jealousy and soon hatred, increased by the mutual wars, still more by this war.
The South German, plundered, cannot look upon the calm of the North German without envy, nor without anger, at being abandoned by his fellow Germans in such need and misery.
The North looks down on the South German, seeing that he is so clever, so shrewd and so fortunate.
zh: D. 对最高权力的信任和服从，在德意志各国家分离的情况下必然不可能。
皇帝所归属的那个民族，不论是奥地利还是巴伐利亚还是勃兰登堡，它和它周围〔各民族〕的语言，别人根本连懂都不懂。
在信任这一方面，权利的差别是一个惊人的疏远之源；〔正如〕受捐税压迫较少的人、比较自由的人，凌驾于农奴之上，另一个人〔感到〕嫉妒、很快又感到仇恨，这种情绪被相互的战争放大，又被这场战争放大得更多。
被抢掠过的南德人，看着北德人的安宁，不可能不眼红，也不可能不愤怒：在这样困苦悲惨的时候，自己竟被自己的德意志同胞丢下不管。
北方人则看不起南德人，因为他觉得自己那么聪明、那么机灵、那么走运。

en: E. Progress since the Peace of Westphalia.
zh: E. 自《威斯特伐利亚和约》以来的进程。

en: Civil wars in England for two royal families.
zh: 英国为两个王室打的内战。

en: Provincial estates, decline of their power ...
zh: 地方等级，其权力的衰落……

en: [Justice]
zh: 〔司法〕

en: In the German Empire there are no state officials - hereditary steward etc. The citizen demands security of property and the care of justice, as few levies as possible - he lets the state provide for everything; the official too, see connection, see relation to the whole etc., he seeks his bread.
Formerly every free man wanted to have a share in it.
Now a class in which the duties of the state have become private rights.
In this separation from the state lies the possibility of forming a state.
zh: 在德意志帝国里没有国家官员——世袭御膳官等等。市民要求财产有保障、司法有人管，捐税尽可能少——他让国家去照管一切；官员也一样，见关联，见对整体的关系等等，他要挣自己的面包。
从前每一个自由人都想在这上面有一份。
现在则是一个等级，在其中，国家的义务变成了私人的权利。
在这种同国家的分离里，存在着形成一个国家的可能性。

en: I recently read Lessing's correspondence with his wife187); - the feeling that I had partly during the reading, partly kept back afterwards, was quite peculiar; it was interest mixed with pleasure and melancholy; after a long course of novel-reading nothing can come more welcome than such a conversation taken wholly from real life.

One is always eager for the development; although no intrigue and great obstacles hold up the development - usual requirements in a novel, in order to stretch the reader's attention -, the interest is nonetheless never lacking and is so much the warmer and more sympathetic because the circumstances are so entirely natural and human; the only obstacle that puts itself in the way concerns the point that nowadays counts most, often almost alone (here, to be sure, not), namely a sufficient livelihood (for love is never so strong that one moves with one another into wildernesses, renounces all comforts and lives only on love), and since that requirement was not yet sufficiently secured, the union is always put off. - No cruel father, no harsh uncle or guardian, no lord pursuing innocence is it that holds up the marriage; the time during which the correspondence continues is six years - what a long time for a bridegroom and a bride! -, and in this interval almost nothing but vexation and suffering through illnesses, and then the duration of the marriage - was only three years; do not reflections on the nullity of man and of his pleasantest cares strike one here? - Should one not think, if a man knew this in advance, would he [then] not prefer an earlier death than nature has appointed for him to such a life? - Perhaps, if one imagines a life full of nothing but misery and hardship, - but one does not take into account what life in concreto is, [rather] the pleasant habit of working and being active, as Goethe calls it, - the incessant influx of feelings into bodily comfort that keeps us constantly occupied; - in a man who can carry out the thought of placing himself outside all these relations, the representations and the working of the soul must go almost solely inward, and the bond that through the senses ties him to the whole of nature must be very weak. - But to come back from this digression to Lessing's correspondence, the whole tone of it, at least for the most part, is more suited to attune the reader to melancholy than to pleasant feeling. - But the language of pain and of sufferings is much more eloquent than the language of joy, and the enjoyment of the latter is not so noticeable as the feeling of the former.

The gloomy moment in which we write draws a black veil also over the memory of happy hours, besides that it brings out the sad still more, lays on stronger colors and puts too much shadow into the painting. - Often a small - secret, unnoticed by the infected person himself - vanity also mixes into the play, which persuades us from the hindmost corner of the heart that it awakens more interest, that the sympathy is greater, when one sees us suffer than when one sees us cheerful, that we appear somewhat greater in pain than in joy etc.

One more remark struck me very much: when Lessing's beloved writes of her bad mood, her vexatious situation and the like and he is just in good humor, he comes along dressed up with rules of life, with precepts from the arte bene vivendi, - as if he had to thank himself, the following of his wise maxims alone, for the cheerful mood into which the circumstances put him (perhaps a beautiful day, joined with the feeling of health). - In this the dear vain little heart often deceives itself. - Through cheerfulness contentment with oneself about one's doings and omissions, about the success of clever plans, about one's external circumstances is promoted; - but one believes that the case is always the reverse, that only when we think we have cause to be content with our conscience, with our prudence, shall the consequence of that be serenity of mind and true pleasure; - as said, mostly it is the reverse; - feeling of health - beautiful weather - freedom from present cares - a prospect of a merry meal puts us into a state of gladness, and this deceives us only too gladly; only misfortune awakens the stings of conscience, piles up the memory of all the thoughtlessnesses to be repented of and seldom lets it rest at having filled the soul with the feeling of the sad situation, of the pains etc., but also calls discontent with oneself, self-accusation to its aid, in order to rob the soul completely of the courage that, steadfast, proud of its innocence, defies the pain. - But here you abolish all distinction between good and evil men?
Only with the latter may the picture you have sketched here fit.
No, but the distinction here is not specific, - but only according to degrees.

Where do we find the man who has the consciousness of having always acted with the best intention, always according to the eternal rule of right and at the same time always with the greatest prudence, and who has nothing to reproach himself with in regard to these points.

Ill humor often calls back things long since done away with, - and however much we often strive to breathe such images quickly away, there nonetheless remains behind the subsequent feeling that mixes with the present ill humor. - But to return to Lessing's moralities, we often find right in the next letter - their efficacy wholly cancelled by circumstances and the most striking proof how little maxims are capable of anything against the impression that relates to pleasure and displeasure. -
zh: 我最近读了莱辛和他妻子的通信187)；——我一部分在阅读时、一部分在事后留在心里的那种感受，很是特别；那是兴趣，掺着愉快和伤感；在长时间读小说之后，没有什么比这样一场完全从现实生活里取来的交谈更让人称心的了。

人总是急于看到事情的发展；虽然没有阴谋和巨大的障碍去挡住这个发展——那是一本小说为绷紧读者的注意力常有的要件——，可兴味从来不缺，而且还要热切得多、共感得多，因为那些情形是那样自然、那样合乎人情；唯一挡在路上的障碍，关系到今天最被看重、往往几乎是唯一被看重的那一点（这里当然不是），也就是足够的生计（因为爱情从来不会强到让人一起搬到荒野里去，抛下一切舒适，只靠爱情活着），而既然那个要件还没有得到足够的保障，结合就总是往后推。——拦住这桩婚事的，不是什么狠心的父亲，不是什么严厉的叔父或监护人，也不是什么追逐纯洁少女的勋爵；通信持续的时间是六年——对未婚夫和未婚妻来说是多么长的时间啊！——而在这段时间里，几乎只有烦恼和疾病带来的痛苦，接着婚姻的持续时间——只有三年；想到这里，人难道不会生出关于人及其最愉快的操心的虚无的思索吗？——人难道不该想：如果一个人事先就知道这一点，他〔就〕不会宁要一个比自然为他规定的更早的死，而不要这样的一生吗？——也许吧，如果人设想的一生全是悲惨和艰辛的话——但人没有把生命 in concreto 是什么算进去，〔毋宁说〕没有把那种愉快的工作和活动的习惯算进去，像歌德所称的那样——那种不断占据我们的、感受持续涌入身体舒适的状态；——在一个能把“把自己置于所有这些关系之外”这个念头付诸实行的人那里，灵魂的表象和活动几乎只能向内去，而通过感官把他同整个自然系在一起的那条纽带，必定非常弱。——不过，从这段离题的话回到莱辛的通信上来，它的整个调子，至少大部分，更适合把读者调向伤感，而不是调向愉快的感受。——但痛苦和受难的语言要比欢乐的语言雄辩得多，而后者的享受也不像前者的感受那样引人注意。
我们写作时那个阴郁的时刻，也给快乐时光的回忆蒙上一层黑纱，何况它还把伤心的事越发衬出来，涂上更重的颜色，往画里放进太多的阴影。——常常还有一点小小的虚荣——隐秘的、连被它传染的人自己也察觉不到的虚荣——混进这场戏里，它从心的最里面的角落说服我们：让我们受苦比让人看见我们快活更能引起兴趣，别人的共感也更大，我们在痛苦里显得比在快乐里要大一些，等等。

还有一点我觉得非常显眼：当莱辛的心上人写到自己的坏脾气、自己恼人的处境之类，而他恰好心情好的时候，他就带着人生规则、带着出自 arte bene vivendi 的训条来了——仿佛他之所以有那种愉快的心情，是情形把他放进去的（也许是一个好天气，加上健康的感受），全得归功于他自己，归功于他对自己那些明智准则的遵行。——在这上面，这颗亲爱又虚荣的小心儿常常看错自己。——快活会促进人对自己满意：对自己的所作所为、对聪明计划的成功、对自己的外部处境都满意；——但人们相信事情总是反过来：只有当我们自以为有理由对自己的良心、对自己的精明感到满意时，由此产生的才该是心情的明朗和真正的愉快；——如前面所说，多半是反过来；——健康的感受——好天气——眼下没有忧虑——眼前有一顿快活的饭，就把我们置入一种欢喜的状态，而这种状态太容易骗我们；只有不幸才唤醒良心的芒刺，把一切要后悔的轻率之举的记忆堆到一起，而且很少就停在让灵魂充满对悲惨处境、对痛苦等等的感受上，还要叫来对自己的不满、自责来帮忙，把灵魂最后一点勇气也夺走——那种坚定地、以自己无辜为傲地对抗痛苦的勇气。——可你这不是把好人和坏人之间的一切区别都取消了吗？
你在这里勾出的那幅画，也许只适用于后一种人。
不，但这里的区别不是种类上的——而只是程度上的。
我们在哪里能找到这样一个人：他意识到自己始终怀着最好的意图、始终依照权利的永恒规则、同时又始终以最大的精明行事，并且在这些方面没有什么可以责备自己的？
坏情绪常常把早已了结的事情召回来——不管我们多么努力想把这类景象赶快吹散，那种随之而来、同眼下坏情绪混在一起的感受还是留在心里。——不过，回到莱辛的道德说教上来，我们常常就在紧接着的一封信里发现——它们的效力被情形完全抵消掉了，并且看到最显眼的证据，说明准则对那种同愉快和不快相关的印象实在没有多大力量。——

en: The tone of the letters is mutual sympathy, communication of his affairs and business, of his grief and his joy - and participation in it on the other side. - The expression is unaffected and stays with the general, - it does not dissect the feeling; it gives the total impression, - just as we see it with the Greeks, where a tragedy is not a compendium of empirical psychology in nuce, as often nowadays; - this is nature, - this goes to enjoyment and feeling. - The early circumstances of youth and of education check the impression of nature in us, - we become too much accustomed to the soul occupying itself with itself, - to judging external objects too much according to concepts, not according to the feelings of beauty; - the heart is closed and only the cold, calculating understanding remains left, - which in the end merely sticks to the means and never thinks of the end. - A cutting difference of our customs and our character from the Greek is surely marked out by the fact that the poet who called to the enjoyment of life through remembrance of death: "Man, enjoy your life!" etc., would appear very insipid among us. - How would I be able to enjoy life today if tomorrow death called me away!
zh: 这些信的调子是相互的共感，是把自己事情和事务、自己的忧愁和快乐讲出来——另一边则对此表示关切。——表达是不加雕琢的，停留在一般的东西上——它不去剖析感受；它给出的是总体印象——正如我们在希腊人那里看到的那样：在希腊人那里，一出悲剧不是一部浓缩（in nuce）的经验心理学纲要，而今天常常就是；——这就是自然——自然所求的是享受和感受。——少年时代和教育的早期情形，阻碍了自然在我们身上的印象——我们太习惯于让灵魂忙于自身——太习惯于按照概念去评判外在对象，而不是按照对美的感受；——心关了起来，只剩下冰冷的、精于计算的知性——它到头来只是黏在手段上，从不想起目的。——我们的习俗和性格同希腊人的习俗和性格之间那道刺眼的分界，大概就画在这里：一个诗人如果通过让人想起死来号召人去享受生活——“人啊，享受你的生活！”等等——他在我们这里会显得非常乏味。——如果明天死就来叫我，我今天还怎么能享受生活呢！

en: Only the Greek could enjoy in this way, could take an interest in every being that expresses life and feeling; - everywhere the pure spirit of the Greeks discovered an unaffected relation, in which the heart took part; he shows himself from this side most nobly in their epigrams, he seems to relate to ours as a boy who smells a rose relates to the apothecary who makes rose water out of it.
Chaste purity and lovely modesty seem generally to have been a property of the Greek genius.
zh: 只有希腊人才能这样享受，才能对每一个表现出生命和感受的存在者感兴趣；——希腊人纯粹的精神到处都发现一种不加雕琢的关系，心在其中有一份；从这一面看，他在他们的警句诗里显得最高贵，他同我们的精神的关系，似乎就像闻玫瑰花的男孩同用它做玫瑰水的药剂师的关系。
贞洁的纯粹和可爱的羞怯，看来根本就是希腊天才所固有的一种品性。
